title: Conformal Policy Control
claim: A safe reference policy plus conformal calibration can regulate an optimized policy via rejection sampling, guaranteeing user-specified risk control.
layout: Single wide panel, left-to-right flow, feedback arrows, central calibration plot
description: A wide left-to-right flow diagram. At the left, a brain icon labeled Safe Policy π0 and a database stack of safe prompts feed an Observe telescope icon. Observations split into Train Data and Calibration Data database stacks. Train data goes to Policy Improvement (a dumbbell icon), which produces an Optimized Policy πt shown as a pink brain. A user silhouette with a speech bubble 'Failure rate ≤ α' sits above a central calibration plot. The plot shows pink and teal constraint-risk curves with a dashed red α line and a blue vertical β-hat line. This feeds an Accept-Reject Sampling node with a check/cross icon. The final panel on the right shows overlapping distributions π0 (teal dashed), πt (red dotted) and the regulated policy (blue solid). Teal, pink and blue arrows mark the data flows. A thick blue arrow loops back from the deployed policy to Observe.
caption: An illustration of safe exploration with conformal policy control. Starting with a safe policy $\pi_0$ and safe context prompts $\mathcal{X}_0:=\{x_1, \dots, x_m\}$, we observe the safe policy's actions $a_i$ and corresponding reward $r_i \in \mathbb{R}$ and constraint violation $\ell_i \in \{0, 1\}$. We split the observations into train and calibration data, and optimize the safe policy to obtain $\pi_t$. We then query the user for their constraint violation risk tolerance $\alpha$, and apply conformal risk control to find a bound on the likelihood ratio $\pi_t / \pi_0$ which guarantees the calibrated risk is controlled at level $\alpha$. Finally we apply rejection sampling to probabilistically regulate the optimized policy for deployment and observation, allowing the user to flexibly trade off reward, constraint risk, and test-time compute.
abstract: An agent must try new behaviors to explore and improve. In high-stakes environments, an agent that violates safety constraints may cause harm and must be taken offline, curtailing any future interaction. Imitating old behavior is safe, but excessive conservatism discourages exploration. How much behavior change is too much? We show how to use any safe reference policy as a probabilistic regulator for any optimized but untested policy. Conformal calibration on data from the safe policy determines how aggressively the new policy can act, while provably enforcing the user's declared risk tolerance. Unlike conservative optimization methods, we do not assume the user has identified the correct model class nor tuned any hyperparameters. Unlike previous conformal methods, our theory provides finite-sample guarantees even for non-monotonic bounded loss functions, and it introduces a new policy control setting. Our experiments on applications ranging from natural language question answering to biomolecular engineering show that safe exploration is not only possible from the first moment of deployment, but can also improve performance.
